name: OOMKilled
root_cause: The worker has its memory leak enabled (MEMORY_LEAK_ENABLED=true): every processed job retains about 1MB that is never released. Its memory limit is 96Mi, only about 45MiB above its idle footprint, so after a few dozen processed jobs the container exceeds the limit and the kernel OOM-kills it.
observable_signals: The worker pod has restarted: RESTARTS is at least 1, and its last state is Terminated with reason OOMKilled and exit code 137
The previous container's logs (kubectl logs --previous) show normal 'Processing order_id=...' lines that stop abruptly, with no exception or traceback
The worker Deployment spec shows MEMORY_LEAK_ENABLED=true and a memory limit of 96Mi
Every other service (gateway, orders, inventory, redis, postgres) is healthy; only the worker is affected
An order whose job was in flight when the container was killed may stay in 'created' status and never become 'fulfilled'
accepted_remediations: Set MEMORY_LEAK_ENABLED back to false on deployment/worker (removes the leak)
Roll back deployment/worker to its previous revision (restores both the leak flag and the original memory limit)
Raise the worker's memory limit (mitigation only: the leak remains, so it will eventually be OOM-killed again at a higher job count)
ineffective_remediations: Restart the worker pod or Deployment: memory resets, but the leak returns as soon as it processes jobs again
Scale deployment/worker up: every replica leaks at the same rate per job, so each is OOM-killed too
Flush or trim the Redis queue: the leak grows with jobs processed, not with queue backlog
Restart or redeploy other services (orders, gateway, inventory, redis, postgres): they are healthy and unrelated
